## Summary

- Evaluated **LISFLOOD-FP** and **SFINCS** as candidate 2D solvers for automated, reach-based FIM
- **Both models meet all project requirements**
- Automation code implemented for each, driven from a common internal data model
- Most differences between the two are configuration semantics
- A smaller set of differences are fundamental and conceptual, with no direct equivalent in the other model:
  - How the active domain is defined and boundary roles are assigned
  - How spatial inputs are stored and indexed
  - Where boundary conditions can be placed

# LISFLOOD-FP

## Core Files

| File | Format | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `<run_id>.par` | ASCII key-value | Main configuration |
| `<run_id>.bci` | ASCII | Boundary condition locations and types |
| `<DEMfile>` | ARC ASCII raster | Terrain |
| `<manningfile>` | ARC ASCII raster | Manning's n |
| `<startfile>` | ARC ASCII raster | Hot-start water depth (optional) |

## File Formats

- Spatial inputs are **ARC ASCII rasters** referenced by path in `.par`
- Configuration and BC files use plain **ASCII key-value** or tabular formats
- NetCDF output is available but was not evaluated — worth investigating for GIS integration and post-processing

## Boundary Conditions — Normal Depth

- `FREE` applies a **normal depth (uniform flow)** condition at edge cells
- Applies **only to edge cells** — cannot be placed in the domain interior
- One-way: water cannot re-enter through a `FREE` cell
- Physics: Manning's equation flux using **local simulated water depth** at each timestep
- Parameterized by a constant friction slope per cardinal direction (`N`, `S`, `E`, `W`)


## Boundary Conditions — Inflow

Inflow is specified as point sources in the `.bci` file:

```
P  x  y  QFIX  value
```

- `value` is discharge per unit width (**m²/s**); LISFLOOD multiplies by cell width internally
- Can be placed on **any cell** in the domain, not just edge cells
- Time-varying inflow (`QVAR` + `.bdy`) is supported but not currently used

## Boundary Conditions — Known WSE

- `HFIX` — constant prescribed WSE on any grid cell
- `HVAR` — time-varying WSE paired with a `.bdy` file
- We use `HFIX` for all stage transfer boundaries, with WSE taken from downstream model results

## Build and Deployment

- Must be **compiled from source**
- Fork maintained at [github.com/Dewberry/lisflood-fp](https://github.com/Dewberry/lisflood-fp) — includes all project patches
- Docker container wrapping the compiled binary used for cloud execution
- GPU acceleration available for acceleration, FV1, and DG2 solvers (requires CUDA compilation)

| Image | Size |
|---|---|
| CPU | 1.1 GB |
| GPU | 3.5 GB |

# SFINCS

## Core Files

| File | Format | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sfincs.inp` | ASCII key=value | Main configuration |
| `sfincs.msk` | Binary uint8 | Cell activity mask |
| `sfincs.ind` | Binary uint32 | Active cell index (binary mode) |
| `sfincs.dep` | Binary float32 | Terrain (active cells only) |
| `sfincs.man` | Binary float32 | Manning's n (active cells only) |
| `sfincs.src` / `sfincs.dis` | ASCII | Inflow points / discharge time series |
| `sfincs.bnd` / `sfincs.bzs` | ASCII | WL boundary coordinates / time series |
| `sfincs.bdr` | ASCII | Normal depth BC definition |

## File Formats

- Spatial inputs can be **binary or ASCII**; binary (`inputformat = bin`) strongly preferred for production
- Binary stores only active cells in **Fortran column-major order** — smaller files, faster reads
- NetCDF input supported from v2024.01 — strong candidate for future adoption; would provide CF-compliant inputs with embedded CRS metadata and eliminate the index file

::: {.callout-warning}
SFINCS NetCDF **outputs are currently bugged** — post-processing is required to convert model results to usable GeoTIFFs before any downstream analysis or delivery.
:::

## The Mask File

SFINCS classifies every grid cell **before the simulation begins** via `sfincs.msk` — there is no direct equivalent in LISFLOOD-FP.

- Defines the **active domain** and **assigns boundary roles** simultaneously
- All spatial inputs store values only for cells where `msk > 0`

![Fig. 14 — SFINCS mask value layout (sfincs.readthedocs.io)](https://sfincs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/_images/SFINCS_mask_grid.PNG){width=80% fig-align="center"}

## Boundary Conditions — Normal Depth

Defined in `sfincs.bdr` as a thalweg line with a slope value (`xb yb xi yi slope d`). SFINCS fits a water surface to the line and enforces the resulting WSE at all mask=5 cells:

$$z_s = z_i - d \times \text{slope}$$

- Can be assigned to **any grid cell**, not just edge cells
- `d = -1` → auto straight-line distance; positive `d` → manual along-channel distance (preferred for sinuous reaches)

## Boundary Conditions — Inflow

- Each cell intersecting the inflow line → one source point in `sfincs.src` with its own discharge column in `sfincs.dis`
- Discharge in **m³/s per cell**
- Can be placed on **any cell** in the domain, not just edge cells

## Boundary Conditions — Known WSE

- Cells designated **mask=2**; coordinates in `sfincs.bnd`, values in `sfincs.bzs`
- Can be assigned to **any grid cell**
- Values can be specified at coarser resolution than the grid — SFINCS interpolates to individual boundary cells using **IDW**


## Build and Deployment

- **Pre-built Docker images** on DockerHub (CPU + GPU) — no compilation required
- GPU acceleration results on `aws g4dn.xlarge`:

| Mode | Size | Runtime |
|---|---|---|
| CPU | 507 MB | ~383 s |
| GPU | 2.8 GB | ~28 s (~14×) |

# Conclusion

## Both Models Are Approved

- Both approved for production use in the automated reach-based FIM pipeline
- Each satisfies all core requirements:
  - Structured grid inputs and outputs
  - GPU acceleration
  - Linux-native, container-based deployment
  - Inflow, stage transfer (known WSE), and normal depth outflow BCs
- A technical report with full implementation details, parameter tables, and gotchas is available as a PDF
